subject: default prior for xi (shape param) in gev model

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: default prior for xi (shape param) in gev model
parts:
Hi Havard et al,

I was playing around with the GEV model and am confused about the prior for xi.  The documentation says theta2 ~ N(0,6.25) where 6.25 is the precision.  So that means that xi = s*theta2, for s=0.01, is normal with mean 0 and sd .01*sqrt(1/6.25) = .004.  This seems quite restrictive and in the example fit shown in the documentation, I actually get a posterior  for what appears to be xi that has 95% CI of roughly (-.75,.75) [see below], which is not consistent with this prior.  Am I missing something or is there a typo in the documentation?

thanks!
Chris

> formula = y ~ 1 + f(inla.group(z), model="rw1")
> data = data.frame(y,z)
> r = inla(formula, data = data, family = "gev",
+         control.data = list(gev.scale.xi = 0.01,
+                 ## just to show how to set an initial value
+                 hyper = list(prec=list(initial=2))))

Hi.

Nice to hear from you!

xi = xi.scale * theta2, and what you get is the posterior for theta2,
and
*not* xi

the prior is also for theta2, not xi.

does this resolvs the issue?

I don't have much experience with the gev-model, and if you have
suggestions to other default parameters, please let me know...

Best,
H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] default prior for xi (shape param) in gev model
parts:
Hi Havard, thanks for the quick response.

I think I see now.... A couple comments...

1) so you report the posterior for theta2 (the reparameterization of
xi) but the posterior for the original tau (i.e., not theta1)? In the
example the posterior mean for the precision is about 4 which is the
true tau, not theta1. That was part of my confusion - I saw that tau
was reported (the original parameterization) and therefore assumed xi
was reported.

2) I think that prior on xi as the default might be fairly narrow, but
don't have a lot of experience with GEVs either. But for
precipitation extremes, my sense is that that prior is too narrow.
Obviously the user can change it and something has to be the default
though.

Chris
